$description: The Health OS reference catalogue. One entry per token group, component, widget, pattern and asset library: what it is for, when to use it, when not to, and its API. The reference site renders these entries next to each live example, and scripts/docs.mjs generates design-system/REFERENCE.md from the same file, so the site and the written reference never disagree. Edit here, then run `npm run docs`.

checklist: Every colour, size, radius, shadow and duration comes from a token. No hex codes or pixel values typed by hand.
The page uses one theme: light or paper. Nothing sits on a dark or carbon background.
Every H1 is a two-tone headline: the point in ink-900, the rest in ink-400, with two or three picture tiles that literally show what it says.
Other headings use the heading or subheading role in ink-900, running text uses body, small text uses label.
Rose, apricot and lavender appear only in their 50, 200 and 400 shades, and text stays in the ink neutrals. Status colours report real states only.
Apricot is the only interactive accent: buttons, links, ticks, toggles, selected states and focus rings are apricot, never rose or lavender.
At most one gradient moment per view, using one of the three gradients, and never a saturated gradient as a large fill.
Widgets and cards use the light (200) and soft (50) shades only, and every button fill is apricot-200 #F8C39C with ink text.
There is one primary button per view. Other actions are secondary or text.
Cards are the right type for their job: content, feature, service, pricing, resource, action, session, profile or steps.
Images come from the tagged library, match their suggested use, dissolve into their card with the shared image fade, and text never sits on a raw photo.
Screenshots are cropped to the point, framed on a surface, and show no private or client information.
Copy is plain Australian English in sentence case, with no em dashes and no invented numbers.
Prices, offers and claims match the Health OS database. No testimonials, countdown pressure or before-and-after images.
Motion is calm, and nothing people need is hidden until an animation finishes.
Anything outside the system has a defined need, is documented, and has Tumai's approval.

open.question: Keep md 8px, lg 12px and full, or return to the earlier 8px cap?
open.current: Provisional: md 8px for controls, lg 12px for containers, full for round things only. No pill buttons.

open.question: Which word does copy use for the customer: operator, practitioner or something else?
open.current: The database says operator. Demo copy in this system says you and clients, and names neither.

open.question: Sage 70 / Creator 30, or Creator 70 / Explorer 30?
open.current: Not used anywhere in this system until decided.

open.question: Which filled icon set, in which two sizes?
open.current: The Icons section is intentionally empty. Components still use Lucide line icons until the set is chosen.

open.question: What should motion do when someone has reduced motion switched on?
open.current: Unchanged from before the cleanup: loops stop and entrances settle instantly. Not an approved policy.

open.question: Commission true vector files for the mark and the long logo?
open.current: The 500px PNG mark and the two 1120 × 400 long logo PNGs (white and filled background) are the usable files. The SVG embeds PNG rasters and is not a vector.

open.question: Polish, keep or delete the five experimental widgets?
open.current: 05 Live session timer, 08 Countdown, 29 Rating summary, 30 Assistant message and 31 Check-in are on and labelled.

open.question: Keep the stack comparison pattern alongside the database rule on comparisons?
open.current: Kept without competitor names or prices. It compares a typical stack of separate tools with one system.

open.question: Act on the tagging notes, or keep everything exactly as it is?
open.current: All 169 images kept. Notes flag 17 byte-identical pairs, visible third-party lettering, two photos showing a Health OS cap and some off-palette backgrounds.

open.question: Keep Certified, Therapeutic grade and Ethically sourced as badge examples?
open.current: Kept as requested. Use them only for a business's own verifiable facts, never as a claim about Health OS.

open.question: Replace the coded dashboard preview with a real, cropped product screenshot?
open.current: The command hero shows a coded mock of the dashboard with sample data.

entries.name: Brand colours
entries.purpose: Sunlit Apricot, Expressive Rose and Neutral Lavender. Each stops at full strength (400) with two lighter shades (200, 50). Apricot is the one interactive accent; rose and lavender carry categories and charts. Widgets and cards use only the lighter two, so colour always reads soft and calm.
use: apricot-200 #F8C39C for every button fill, checked checkbox, radio and switch, selected state, tab underline and link underline, with ink text
apricot-50 with an apricot-200 edge for selected rows, chips, filters and the active navigation item
apricot-400 for focus rings, focused field borders and thin marks such as the / in a command chip
Rose and lavender 200 and 50 for categories, badges, chart data, icons and tiles in widgets and cards
400 of rose and lavender only for gradient stops and category dots
avoid: Rose or lavender for anything interactive: buttons, links, ticks, toggles, selected states or focus
Full-strength colour inside a widget, card or button
Coloured text: text stays in the ink neutrals
Any shade darker than 400, or shades outside 50, 200 and 400

ink-100 and ink-200 for quiet fills, dividers and pressed states
carbon/60 and carbon/80 for the video control bar, carbon/40 for the modal backdrop
avoid: ink-400 for body text or anything smaller than a heading
Carbon, black or any dark colour as a background: panels, footers, banners, tooltips, tiles or logo grounds
Pure black or hand-coded white as a page ground
